review_notes: I read the whole file (lines 1–129) and judged it against the rubric using the text alone. I did not open Mathlib, the Complexitylib sources or the imported files. The file has two groups of repeated proofs. (1) Eight `*_mem_FP` theorems share the shape `simpa only [def] using! machinePair{First,Second}_mem_FP`. Each is a one-line unfold-and-reuse wrapper around an existing theorem. (2) The `*_pair`, `*_encode` and `*_cons` simp lemmas are each closed by one `simp [...]` call that unfolds definitions. None of these contains nontrivial mathematical reasoning that is repeated. A shared lemma would only replace one-line unfoldings with another one-line call, or would add indirection. The rubric explicitly counts short calculations, routine unfolding and thin wrappers as insufficient. The many aliases (`machineListHead`, `machineMatrixDimensionWord` and similar) might be redundant. That is a different concern from repeated proof machinery, so I did not report it. The only uncertainty is that I did not check the downstream uses.
